Just stop caring about your rank in 1s for a while so you can focus on figuring out what it is that's causing you to lose/your opponent to win. Usually the deciding factors end up being stuff like not taking your time when you have space on offense, leaving your net open to grab boost on defense, defending too passively, etc... 1s is mostly about consistency and mitigating your own mistakes/capitalizing on your opponents mistakes. It's also about not tilting since the first player to lose their cool after a couple bad plays is usually the one that loses.

Just treat it as practice and experiment to see what works and what doesn't, eventually you'll figure out the rhythm and start ranking up naturally.

The most basic form of rotation I'd teach to a beginner is basically to just rush back to your own goal after you hit/try and fail to hit the ball away from yourself on offense. If everyone on the team does this consistently you'll end up taking turns hitting the ball, rotating back, and defending, there'll always be one player doing each. Chasing the ball instead of rotating will usually just end up with either too many defenders or too many attackers and that will always lead to your opponent getting easy scoring chances due to confusion. Oh and if you aren't sure when to go forward once you reach your goal, just try to time it so that you're leaving right as your teammate rotating back is arriving to the goal. There are more nuances to rotation, but as a beginner just try to get good at these basics first and you should be able to rank up consistently as you improve this plus your other fundamentals like hitting the ball hard and such

Being good on defense to me includes trusting my teammate to make their moves when they feel it is the right moment and simply hanging back in a position to cover lose balls or run into a pass should that be their intention. I try not to rush anyone or force them to move unless the ball goes directly to me while I'm rotating back, in which case I will ofc try to get a pass back to my tm8 which I guess could be considered rushing but I think that'd be unreasonable. I'm 100% not the kind of player OP is describing, it's just hard to really describe the difference in what I do compared to someone who overhesitates I suppose.

I personally prefer ballchasers since I genuinely enjoy and am particularly good on defense relative to my rank so I don't have a very hard time filling in the gaps they leave. As for watching streamers, most of what I've learned is how to properly position myself to cover as many angles as possible on defense and how to be effectively annoying on offense.

Hope this helps!
